location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:1
text: Build a browser management game about delivering communications services across unified communications, contact centres, meetings, CPaaS and the partner ecosystem. The player starts as a communications MSP, assembles services from vendors and specialists, and expands into service-provider and programmable-communications offerings.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:3
text: The core loop is **win a contract → discover requirements → assemble an eligible service → deploy or migrate → prove outcomes → operate → renew and expand**. A successful service must satisfy its technical, operational, information-handling and commercial requirements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:5
text: This design extends the Series of Tubes fork concept across SMB, enterprise, government and defence customers. Product references are dated to **29 October 2026**. Scenario sizes, demand curves, prices, quality parameters and market effects are game-design assumptions; real product capabilities and lifecycle facts are identified through their linked sources.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:7
text: # Product structure and player experience

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:9
text: Keep four dimensions separate.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:11
text: | Dimension | Values and purpose |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:11
text: | Customer profile | SMB, enterprise, government and defence campaign archetypes, with separate size, sector, jurisdiction, sensitivity and user-persona fields |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:11
text: | Workload | Employee calling, collaboration, meetings, events, customer service, outbound engagement, embedded communications and critical notifications |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:11
text: | Delivery | Shared public cloud, dedicated hosted service, partner-operated private cloud, on-premises, hybrid and explicitly disconnected deployments |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:11
text: | Commercial role | Vendor, distributor, reseller, integrator, MSP, carrier or service provider, CPaaS supplier or application builder, and contact-centre operator or BPO |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:18
text: An organisation can have several roles. A carrier can also provide managed services; an MSP can resell a platform and subcontract contact-centre operations. SMB and enterprise describe scale, while government and defence describe sector and workload requirements. Preserve those distinctions underneath the four campaign choices.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:20
text: The player initially controls a single MSP. Vendors, carriers, integrators, developers and BPOs are commercial counterparts. Wholesale operations, CPaaS products and staffed contact-centre operations unlock later. Staffing controls should only become available when the player or its subcontractor is responsible for that workforce.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:22
text: Use four principal views:

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:24
text: 1. **Customer and contracts:** needs, budget, procurement, obligations, renewals and satisfaction.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:26
text: 2. **Service topology:** sites, platforms, rooms, carriers, integrations, storage and trust boundaries.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:28
text: 3. **Operations:** incidents, service journeys, workforce bottlenecks, changes and test evidence.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:30
text: 4. **Business:** recurring and project income, upstream costs, staffing, usage and margin.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:32
text: The signature diagnostic tool is the **interaction inspector**. It follows a customer need through channel choice, service dependencies, human or AI handling, generated information, resolution and cost. Voice interactions retain separate signalling and bidirectional media traces. Meeting interactions expose identity, calendar, room mode, joining, media and artefact dependencies. Messaging interactions expose channel eligibility, delivery, routing, context and human handoff.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:85
text: The [ACS retirement and breaking-changes guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/communication-services/acs-retirement-and-breaking-changes-guide) sets **30 September 2028** as the transition date for standalone ACS retirement and related SDK changes. location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:87
text: [Copilot in Teams documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/copilot-teams-transcription) distinguishes temporary speech processing from saved transcription and states that Copilot is unavailable in end-to-end encrypted meetings. Model that conflict for the relevant profile. Do not make it a universal rule covering every vendor or future version.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:89
text: The documented [Teams Rooms Pro integration with ServiceNow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/microsoft-teams-rooms-configure-servicenow) is Commercial-cloud-only. This is an example of an operational integration whose availability differs from that of the underlying room device.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:154

text: [Otter](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/4425393298327-Otter-Notetaker-Overview), [Fireflies](https://guide.fireflies.ai/articles/5365127863-web-conference-platforms-supported) and [Read AI](https://support.read.ai/hc/en-us/articles/44022838331667-Connecting-Read-AI-to-Microsoft-Teams) demonstrate meeting-assistant integrations. location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:185
text: A contract records seller, buyer, offer, unit of charge, included allowance, overage, minimum commitment, service obligations, support owner, renewal and exit terms. Track seat, room, named agent, concurrent agent, session, minute, message, API transaction and project fees as distinct units.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:187
text: For a player-owned MSP, retail customer payments are income; wholesale, licence, channel, staff and support payments are costs. Eliminate internal transfers when consolidating player-owned subsidiaries. A bundled allowance must be consumed before overage is added.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:189
text: Partner qualifications unlock defined offers or responsibilities. A qualification does not confer every integration or government approval. Cisco's [wholesale guide](https://help.webex.com/article/nwwg3w6) provides a concrete example of parent partners, subpartners, customer onboarding and billing responsibilities.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:191
text: Commercial events include renewal pressure, minimum-commitment exposure, vendor-direct sales, partner acquisition, API changes, supply shortages and product retirement. Each event changes an identifiable offer, relationship or dependency, with visible lead times and available responses.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:193
text: # Customer segments and procurement

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:195
text: Use these four campaign archetypes while retaining their underlying dimensions.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:197
text: | Segment | Typical goals | Possible mandatory requirements | Example contract |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:197
text: | SMB | Fast setup, predictable cost, limited administration, familiar customer channels | Required coverage, existing workflows, business hours and essential devices | A service business needs phones, a small queue, WhatsApp enquiries and reminders |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:197
text: | Enterprise | Multi-site integration, continuity, user adoption, automation and operating cost | Required journeys, identity, recording, geography and support terms | An acquisition introduces another UC and room estate |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:197
text: | Government | Accessible public services, records, controlled access, procurement and continuity | Specified environment, data handling, administrative boundaries and evidence | A citizen contact service spanning phone, web and digital channels |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:197
text: | Defence | Workload suitability, controlled information flows, resilient operation and assured support | Scenario-defined sensitivity boundary, authorised components and disconnected operation where required | Separate administrative collaboration and a locally operated training environment |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:204
text: Apply industry overlays such as healthcare, financial services, education, retail, hospitality and critical infrastructure. A small regulated business can have stronger handling requirements than a large ordinary enterprise.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:206
text: The bid evaluator first checks mandatory requirements. It then compares eligible designs on price, usability, resilience, integration, implementation effort and supportability. Show the player which requirement blocks a design and which alternatives are available.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:208
text: Government and defence contracts need jurisdiction-specific content packs. US cloud labels are not universal approvals for Australia, Europe or other regions. Public-service external channels and restricted internal workloads may belong in different service environments within the same organisation.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:210
text: A defence scenario should distinguish administrative and training workloads from more restricted services. Restricted information should only traverse explicit, scenario-permitted interfaces. The game can explore continuity, access and approved workflows without modelling real operational secrets.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:212
text: # Competition and channel substitution

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:214
text: Model the underlying need before the chosen channel: reach a colleague, resolve a billing issue, attend a meeting, receive a notification or complete an application workflow. The same need can be served through several eligible channels.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | Pressure | Demand that may change | Opportunity for the player |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | WhatsApp and Messenger | Customer enquiries, confirmations and routine notifications | Channel integration, automated journeys, CRM context and human handoff |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | Slack and persistent collaboration | Internal calls, short meetings and email exchanges | Governance, identity, external collaboration, archives and integrations |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | Zoom, Google Meet and bundled conferencing | Meetings, room-platform preference and associated seats | Interoperability, room deployment, adoption and managed operations |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | CPaaS and embedded experiences | Communications move inside booking, commerce or support applications | APIs, workflow development, testing and service assurance |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | AI self-service | Some routine human handling | Reliable automation, escalation, evaluation and new customer-service offers |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:216
text: | Vendor bundles and direct sales | Standalone features lose their separate commercial premium | Specialisation, integration, operating service and portfolio adjustment |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:225
text: These effects are scenario parameters, not current market-share claims. Allow customers to use several platforms simultaneously. Switching has contract, migration, training, integration and data costs. Retention and adoption change with experienced outcomes over time.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:227
text: [WhatsApp's pricing documentation](https://business.whatsapp.com/products/platform-pricing) distinguishes delivered-message categories and free service responses within its customer-service rules. The game should account for the relevant channel economics rather than assuming every message has the same cost. [Webex Connect](https://help.webexconnect.io/docs/welcome) demonstrates that WhatsApp and Messenger can also be components of a commercial engagement platform.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:229
text: Slack provides huddles and meeting-note capabilities, while [Zoom's portfolio](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/) spans several collaboration and customer-service products. Treat substitution by job and capability; a competing meeting product need not replace PSTN or specialised customer-service requirements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:231
text: Examples of market events:

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:233
text: - Messaging adoption shifts routine enquiries away from voice and creates a digital backlog.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:235
text: - A messaging outage redirects unresolved cases into the voice queue.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:237
text: - A suite adds an included feature, reducing the price customers will pay for a separate add-on.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:239
text: - A customer standardises employee collaboration but retains a specialist contact centre.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:241
text: - A platform retirement creates a migration programme across application workflows and numbers.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:243
text: Competition should offer choices to integrate, rebundle, specialise, improve service or accept reduced demand. Avoid unexplained percentage losses that the player cannot investigate.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:245
text: # Contact centre and customer journey simulation

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:247
text: Contact-centre success depends on both technical service and available human or automated work.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:249
text: Track arrival profiles by channel, skills and languages, agent shifts, availability, handling time, after-contact work, queue policy, callbacks, transfers, escalation and repeat contacts. Model digital concurrency separately from synchronous voice handling.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:251
text: Keep these capacities independent:

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:253
text: - Human agent time and relevant skills.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:255
text: - Concurrent-agent or named-agent entitlements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:257
text: - Trunk and SBC sessions.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:259
text: - IVR and media resources.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:261
text: - Network bandwidth and quality.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:263
text: - Bot or transcription compute.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:265
text: - API throughput and downstream application availability.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:267
text: More trunks do not solve a shortage of trained staff. Additional staff do not repair an unavailable CRM connector or media path. If the player only supplies technology, staff capacity is a customer constraint; if it contracts a BPO or operates the centre, staffing becomes a direct decision.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:269
text: Use an interaction state machine with arrival, eligibility, routing, self-service, queueing, handling, wrap-up and resolved or unresolved outcomes. Asynchronous conversations can pause and resume without occupying a voice session throughout.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:271
text: Customer-facing metrics should include resolution, first-contact resolution, waiting, abandonment, repeat contact, customer effort and satisfaction, alongside cost and handling time. A bot that avoids a human transfer but fails the task should create dissatisfaction or repeat demand. A resolved issue with a failed mandatory recording is still an incomplete contracted service.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:273
text: Preserve journey identity across channels. A customer moving from WhatsApp to voice should retain its case context when the configured integration supports that path. If context is lost, handling time and customer effort rise.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:275
text: Useful incidents include broken CRM screen-pop, stale workforce forecasts, bot handoff loops, missing language skills, callback failures, inaccessible recordings and faulty identity mapping after migration. [Genesys WEM](https://help.genesys.cloud/articles/about-workforce-engagement-management-wem/) illustrates the separate workforce, quality and recording functions around the core contact-centre platform.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:277
text: # Transcription AI and information handling

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:279
text: Treat recording, captions, durable transcripts, translations, summaries, action items and search indexes as different artefacts.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:281
text: For each artefact, track the source interaction, participants, capture permission, processing service and location, storage and backup locations, access policy, retention, export destinations and links to derived artefacts. The availability of a transcription capability does not establish that the customer permits its use.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:283
text: The processing chain can include capture, speech recognition, speaker attribution, translation, redaction, summarisation, customer-record update, archive and search. Each stage has capacity, cost, latency, quality and handling requirements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:285
text: Provide both platform-native and specialist integrations. Hosted speech services and local inference have different operating obligations. [Deepgram's deployment documentation](https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/deployment-options) distinguishes hosted and customer-operated deployment; [Microsoft's disconnected container documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/containers/disconnected-containers) identifies supported services and access requirements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:287
text: A third-party meeting assistant can offer cross-platform value while adding another processor, identity and export path. [Fireflies](https://guide.fireflies.ai/articles/5365127863-web-conference-platforms-supported) and [Read AI's Teams integration](https://support.read.ai/hc/en-us/articles/44022838331667-Connecting-Read-AI-to-Microsoft-Teams) provide concrete reference examples.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:289
text: The initial engine can simulate accuracy, language support, processing capacity and escalation through explicit parameters and seeded outcomes. A live model is unnecessary for the game loop. If an optional tutor is added later, it should explain engine evidence rather than decide whether a service works.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:291
text: # Sovereignty and disconnected operation

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:293
text: Evaluate each relevant dependency against the customer's requirements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Dimension | What to inspect |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Storage | Media, messages, recordings, transcripts, logs, metadata, backups and indexes |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Processing | Media relays, transcription, translation, AI inference, analytics and support processing |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Keys | Custody, access to plaintext, recovery and dependent services |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Administration | Who operates the service and who can receive privileged access |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Jurisdiction | The scenario's contractual and workload applicability |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Connectivity | Identity, licensing, management, DNS, time, certificate, update and telemetry dependencies |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Information flow | Permitted data, destinations, interfaces and boundary crossings |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Availability | Behaviour during isolation, failure, maintenance and recovery |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:295
text: | Evidence | Product, edition, version, deployment, region and dated supporting information |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:307
text: Local media, local storage, local AI and disconnected operation are distinct properties. A platform may satisfy one and fail another. The [Cisco AI PODs licensing qualification](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/conferencing/ai-pods-collaboration/ai-pods-collaboration-ds.html) is a useful example of why the entire service chain must be checked.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:309
text: Some requirements should block a bid or feature activation. Price or a generic security score cannot compensate for a prohibited processing destination. Other requirements may be preferences with explicit trade-offs.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:311
text: Give the player meaningful alternatives: select another processor, change the workflow, provide an approved local capability, reduce the promised feature set or decline the contract. The customer should not be forced onto a universal cloud progression.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:313
text: # Engine and content architecture

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:315
text: Retain the static browser shell, canvas interaction, panel infrastructure, persistence patterns and useful tests from [Series of Tubes at commit 48e6200](https://github.com/fjaeckel/seriesoftubes/tree/48e6200c532d486f79bc8376de0aecbf6169123b). The source uses shared state and derived results in an assembled classic script; the expanded domain should have clear function boundaries within that initial architecture. [Upstream architecture](https://github.com/fjaeckel/seriesoftubes/blob/48e6200c532d486f79bc8376de0aecbf6169123b/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:317
text: Keep company ownership, product family, commercial offer and deployed instance distinct. They change for different reasons.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Entity | Responsibility |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Organisation | Ownership, commercial roles, customer or provider relationships |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Customer profile | Scale, sector, jurisdiction, personas, workloads and requirements |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Product and offer | Capabilities, commercial units, included allowances and lifecycle |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Deployment instance | Hosting, version, tenant, resources, region and operating boundaries |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Compatibility edge | Supported interaction or feature, mechanism, prerequisites and limitations |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Contract | Buyer, seller, price, support owner, obligations, renewal and exit |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Service journey | Intended outcome and required interaction and artefact steps |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Interaction | Channel, participants, routing, media, handling and outcome |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Workforce cohort | Skills, schedules, work capacity and operator ownership |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Information artefact | Source, processing, storage, access, retention and derived lineage |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Market event | Changes to demand, products, offers, relationships or availability |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:319
text: | Test evidence | Scenario, journey, observed result, explanation and model version |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:334
text: A compatibility record should include source and target profiles, direction, feature subset, versions, cloud and region, authentication, licences, support owner, evidence URL and checked date. Evidence status can be certified, officially documented, marketplace-listed, vendor-claimed, scenario-tested or unknown. Preserve unknown as unknown.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:336
text: Product capabilities should distinguish available, preview, retiring, retired and unsupported states. Keep dates for new sales, renewals, support and technical compatibility separately. Real vendor reference packs should be pinned to a checked date; fictional campaign packs can use stable balancing assumptions.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:338
text: Suggested engine boundaries are requirements evaluation, dependency resolution, demand generation, interaction routing, call and media calculation, meeting calculation, messaging workflows, contact-centre queues, AI and artefact processing, economics, incident effects and explanation generation.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:340
text: Use aggregate demand for most users and representative interactions for diagnosis. A management tick can advance business time while shorter deterministic event steps handle demand and queues. Preserve scenario seed, clock and stable IDs for reproducibility.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:342
text: The original call resolver remains a specialised part of the interaction engine. Resolve numbers and permissions before call admission, then evaluate signalling and each media direction. Use graph routing only for transport problems where that abstraction is appropriate.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:344
text: Give the fork a new application ID, local-storage namespace, service-worker cache and versioned save schema. Upstream saves have ISP-specific fields and validation. Preserve the original MIT notice and attribution, and update domain, release and analytics assumptions. [Save implementation](https://github.com/fjaeckel/seriesoftubes/blob/48e6200c532d486f79bc8376de0aecbf6169123b/src/game/91-save.js).

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:346
text: The initial deployment remains a static build. Real tenant provisioning, real PSTN calls and live customer information are outside the simulation. All services and interactions are synthetic.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:348
text: # First campaign

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:350
text: Use one fictional regional communications MSP, two platform families, two carriers and a compact specialist-app catalogue. The four customer contracts remain active as the business grows, so earlier decisions continue to generate costs and support obligations.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:352
text: ## Contract one SMB digital service

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:354
text: A small service business needs business calling, a shared number, a modest customer queue, appointment reminders and WhatsApp enquiries.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:356
text: The player chooses a bundle, provisions users and numbers, connects a CPaaS workflow and customer-record integration, and defines human handoff. A demand shift creates more messaging work while the same trained people are occupied with calls.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:358
text: Success requires correctly routed interactions, a functioning customer record, resolved enquiries and sustainable operating cost. The incident teaches the difference between workforce capacity and telecommunications capacity.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:360
text: ## Contract two Enterprise acquisition

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:362
text: An enterprise adds sites using another UC platform, legacy devices and meeting rooms. It needs coexistence, a staged migration, reception features and recorded customer interactions.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:364
text: The player chooses which components to retain, integrates meeting rooms, maps identities and numbers, and moves one cohort at a time. During cutover, voice succeeds while the recorder and room-calendar connector still reference old identities.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:366
text: Success requires complete service journeys, working rooms, preserved evidence and continuity for users on both platforms. This introduces migration, specialists, feature compatibility and operational testing.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:368
text: ## Contract three Government citizen service

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:370
text: A public agency needs phone, web and digital contact, language support, accessibility, defined record handling and a support chain appropriate to the contract.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:372
text: The player builds an eligible service and plans agent skills, permitted processing, recording and retention. A proposed transcription feature would improve wrap-up time but uses a processing location excluded by the contract.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:374
text: Success requires an eligible architecture, usable service, correctly handled artefacts and maintained response targets. The player can choose a different processor, an eligible local service or an agreed reduced feature set.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:376
text: ## Contract four Defence continuity

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:378
text: An administrative and training facility needs a defined collaboration service to continue during external disconnection, with controlled recording or transcription where permitted.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:380
text: The player supplies local communications and meetings, checks identity, time, licensing, certificates and maintenance dependencies, and separates permitted external services. A continuity exercise reveals an overlooked external dependency.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:382
text: Success requires the specified local journeys to continue and information boundaries to hold. The scenario concerns administrative service continuity and contains synthetic information.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:384
text: ## Compact initial catalogue

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:386
text: Implement two UC platform archetypes, one contact-centre module, two carrier profiles, one CPaaS orchestrator, two digital channels, one room-interoperability service, one recorder or archive, one CRM connector, one lifecycle and testing tool, and one local transcription option.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:388
text: Map real Microsoft, Cisco and third-party products into versioned reference packs as feature evidence is established. The initial catalogue should be small enough that each choice has a visible gameplay consequence.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:390
text: # Delivery phases and acceptance

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Phase | Deliverable | Acceptance |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Foundation | Fork baseline, schema, namespaces, capability and evidence model | The renamed shell loads and saves; invalid catalogue relationships are rejected |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Core service | Voice, media, identity, numbers, contracts and inspector | Calls have correct and explainable setup and media outcomes |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Digital customer service | Messaging, CPaaS workflows, queues, human or bot handling and CRM context | The SMB contract is playable, including a workforce bottleneck |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Enterprise change | Coexistence, migration, room joining, recording and specialist apps | The enterprise contract preserves required journeys through change |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Information boundaries | Artefacts, policy checks, local processing and dependency evaluation | Government and defence contracts enforce their explicit requirements |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:392
text: | Market operations | Demand shifts, partner offers, renewals, lifecycle events and balancing | Choices affect sustainable service outcomes and explainable economics |

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:401
text: Use behavioural fixtures covering:

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:403
text: 1. Valid internal and external calls.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:405
text: 2. Number interpretation and ambiguous extensions.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:407
text: 3. Signalling success with a failed media direction.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:409
text: 4. Session exhaustion and configured fallback.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:411
text: 5. A contact-centre staffing bottleneck that remains after a trunk upgrade.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:413
text: 6. An asynchronous message returning to the right customer case.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:415
text: 7. A bot failure that causes repeat demand or escalation.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:417
text: 8. A migration that preserves old-to-new and new-to-old journeys.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:419
text: 9. Successful voice with failed mandatory recording.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:421
text: 10. A healthy room device with broken scheduling or joining dependencies.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:423
text: 11. A third-party integration unavailable in the selected cloud.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:425
text: 12. A transcript processor outside the permitted boundary.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:427
text: 13. A local service with an unsatisfied external dependency.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:429
text: 14. A retiring offer that supports existing service but cannot be newly sold.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:431
text: 15. Included usage and wholesale costs that reconcile without double counting.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:433
text: 16. A competitor-channel demand shift that preserves the underlying customer needs.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:435
text: 17. Reproducible state and outcomes after save, reload and replay.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:437
text: Keep the existing headless harness where useful, with a small real-browser smoke test for topology selection, the inspector, mobile controls and save/reload. [Upstream test harness](https://github.com/fjaeckel/seriesoftubes/blob/48e6200c532d486f79bc8376de0aecbf6169123b/tests/harness.js).

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:439
text: For parallel implementation, assign separate ownership of the domain engine, UI, content catalogue and scenario verification. Agree state and result contracts before parallel edits; keep changes to shared schemas coordinated through one integration owner.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:441
text: # Implementation brief

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:443
text: Build Series of Calls as a communications-ecosystem management-game fork of fjaeckel/seriesoftubes, starting from the inspected 48e6200 baseline. Preserve MIT attribution and the static browser build. Record the baseline build and test results before domain changes.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:445
text: The player begins as a communications MSP and can expand into wholesale/SP and CPaaS services. Model vendor, distributor, reseller, integrator, MSP, carrier, CPaaS and BPO roles separately from customer segments. Provide SMB, enterprise, government and defence campaign profiles with explicit size, sector, jurisdiction, workload and information-handling requirements.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:447
text: Create a capability catalogue, deployment profiles, scoped compatibility edges and contracts. Keep real vendor facts in dated reference packs and gameplay prices and performance assumptions in separate balancing data. Distinguish certification, documentation, listing, vendor claims and scenario evidence.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:449
text: Implement one shared interaction model across voice, meetings and messaging. Preserve separate call signalling and directional media calculations. Add queue and workforce capacity, asynchronous conversations, CRM context, bot handoff, recording and transcript artefacts. Use structured reason chains for the interaction inspector.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:451
text: Mandatory eligibility checks precede commercial scoring. Evaluate processing and storage, support and administrative access, key custody, external dependencies and permitted information flows independently. A vendor brand, local device or marketplace listing cannot satisfy these checks by itself.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:453
text: Provide a consolidated economic ledger with recurring, project, seat, concurrent-agent, session, minute, message and other applicable units. Account for bundle allowances, wholesale costs, staffing and support. Avoid counting the same payment as multiple sources of player profit.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:455
text: Build the four-contract campaign progressively: SMB digital service, enterprise acquisition and migration, government citizen service, and defence administrative continuity. Use a small fictional catalogue first, with Microsoft, Cisco and third-party reference mappings that demonstrate the relevant capabilities.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:457
text: Make market events modify a specific demand profile, offer, contract or dependency. WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack, conferencing and AI can be substitutes and useful components of the solution. Preserve customer journeys and multi-platform adoption.

location: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md:459
text: Use deterministic seeds, simulation time and stable IDs. Keep all calls, messages, customers and telemetry synthetic. Implement behavioural fixtures for failure, recovery, eligibility, economic reconciliation and reproducible save/load. Deliver the browser build, source changes, architecture notes, catalogue schema, scenario guide and verification results.

Synthetic browser configuration training with a communications-business management campaign; guided lessons, assessed challenges and sandbox; outcome and constraint assessment accepts alternative solutions.

Independent public zanefounty/series-of-calls repository without a GitHub fork relationship; preserve all upstream Git history, MIT licence and attribution; origin is the new repository and upstream is fjaeckel/seriesoftubes.
Use latest upstream main and reconcile the original mapping baseline, including save slots, background simulation, automation, puzzles, architect challenges, calendar and MCP.

Preserve both supplied files unchanged, including all JSON metadata, original attributes, predicates, implementation notes, references, counts, 217 file records, findings and limitations; record hashes, provenance and dates.

Every substantive source item requires stable source, requirement, fictional representation, implementation and acceptance IDs. Generated complete appendices accompany explanatory behavioural specifications; semantic fidelity still needs human review.

Gameplay uses fictional organisations, products and channels; all calls, messages, tenants, users and diagnostics remain synthetic. Preserve deployment, connectivity, integration and processing distinctions.

Implement organisation roles, UC/calling, meetings/rooms, contact centre, CPaaS/messaging, third-party applications, AI/information, infrastructure/SP, commercial operations, market dynamics, government and defence.
Separate desired configuration, provisioning progress, effective configuration and observed service state. Each configurable family needs its own appropriate administration workflow and diagnostics.

Inspector explains intent, channel, dependencies, decisions, signalling, directional media, human/automated handling, records, obligations and cost. Synthetic protocol traces derive from actual simulated transitions.
Telecommunications capacity, agent entitlement and available skilled people are independent. Staffing controls follow workforce operating responsibility.

Retain saved state, derived results and validated action dispatch; pure recalculation cannot bill, advance queues or consume randomness. Deterministic clocks, IDs and randomness; aggregate demand and bounded detailed traces; UI, automation and local MCP share command validation.

Independent application, save schema, storage, cache, slot, lock and broadcast identities; clear rejection of ISP saves; version content and jurisdiction packs; worker serialization, stale-result rejection and synchronous fallback.

SMB digital service, enterprise acquisition/migration, government citizen service and defence administrative continuity; Australian, US, Japanese and EU-wide jurisdiction variants. EU-wide rules imply no member-state approvals.
Retain physical network gameplay as an optional SP expansion; an MSP can purchase connectivity.

Executable source integrity, specification coverage, catalogue, acceptance, upstream, freshness and release gates; negative tests for missing mappings/evidence, false completion, invalid relationships, stale upstream and expired jurisdiction reviews.

Weekly and manual checks of pinned main and releases with complete commit/file inventories; last successful check, latest observed, classified, implemented/resolved and outstanding work are distinct. Every change is copy, adapt, already covered or explicitly excluded; exclusions need owner approval and rationale.

Classify within 7 days; ordinary adoption within 30 days; urgent fixes within 7 days; successful check no older than 14 days at release. Pending work permits development; overdue work blocks release. No watchdog or waiver subsystem.

Codex on a GitHub runner, isolated read-only generation and separate trusted bot PR writer; explicit checks for bot PRs, one active run, bounded attempts/time, source/runtime/model/change/test/usage records; leave failures visible. Agent cannot approve exclusions, extend deadlines, raise budgets or weaken gates.

Dedicated API project with enforced US$25 monthly spending limit; keep execution disabled until credentials and enforcement exist. Slight provider overshoot is possible; no exact per-run dollar guarantee. Owner approval for bot changes; owner PRs may bypass review but never required checks. Governance changes need separate owner-reviewed PRs.
Monthly link and material-content observations, historical evidence and reviewer acceptance kept separate; never rewrite gameplay automatically. Active jurisdiction claims reviewed within 90 days.

All supplied mappings, research and upstream additions verified or explicitly approved; reference and failing solutions for all assessed scenarios; browser desktop/mobile, keyboard, offline, replay, worker, concurrency and configuration progression checks; publish only eligible full build to https://zanefounty.github.io/series-of-calls/. Intermediate builds accurately labelled.

Preserve and appropriately transpose the original witty fictional names, comparisons and narrative into mapped communications roles. Keep source provenance, do not let flavour establish technical readiness, and retain outstanding narrative review.

Use cheaper-model agents to research the Cisco VoIP and VoiceOps Puck archives for candidate gameplay issues. Record primary thread evidence, historical uncertainty and proposed fictional acceptance cases; distinguish proposals from adopted requirements.
Complete the full original agreed scope before the first playable handoff. Intermediate builds remain internal checkpoints; do not replace full completion with an early private playtest.

Regenerate coherent witty illustrated operations artwork for launch, four campaigns and optional SP, with responsive assets, installation icons, social preview, provenance and actual browser visual checks. Preserve source-linked humour and clear administration controls.

Run all applicable original-app and adapted-app tests with locked dependencies, both real stdio MCP servers, browser MCP playthroughs and automated real-browser desktop/mobile/offline/keyboard/concurrent-tab tests. No blocked checks, dependency overrides or compact reference exercises count as full campaign acceptance.

Original scope first: retain the 23 already registered operator findings as core obligations; review the 75 archive proposals, but keep additional scenarios in later expansion rather than making every proposal a release requirement.

Candidate observable behavior: When both endpoint profiles accept the negotiated resume offer, signalling and both media directions recover after hold/resume. Negative boundary: When the far endpoint returns an incompatible inactive answer, retain successful signalling but report the affected media leg as inactive and identify the profile interaction; do not claim the historical version behavior is universal. Pending mechanisms: The calling pack reports codec, encryption, NAT and quality dimensions. The core can show signalling success with failed media, but does not model hold/resume SDP negotiation or endpoint-specific offer/answer contracts. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:media, uc-new:domain:signalling.

Candidate observable behavior: A compatible early-offer profile completes the blind transfer and both endpoints report media in both directions. Negative boundary: A direction mismatch leaves the destination leg one-way while signalling remains established; the diagnosis names the synthetic leg/profile and does not prescribe header rewriting as universally safe. Pending mechanisms: The core supports blind transfer journeys only in narrow forms and the calling pack models directional media, but not transfer-leg SDP renegotiation or trunk-profile-specific behavior. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:media, uc-new:domain:signalling, uc-new:domain:continuity.

Candidate observable behavior: With a compatible firmware profile, selecting the monitored destination while transfer is pending completes the original call transfer. Negative boundary: With an incompatible firmware profile, the same key starts a second call and leaves the first transfer pending; manual dialing remains a distinct diagnostic control. Pending mechanisms: The core's transfer flow does not model BLF/presence buttons, endpoint key sequences or firmware-gated transfer behavior. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:continuity, uc-new:family:cisco:dedicated-premises.

Candidate observable behavior: A request arriving at an allowed trunk node matches the configured service and proceeds to dial-plan evaluation. Negative boundary: A request delivered to a disallowed node returns a synthetic device-handler rejection even when the destination number is valid; adjusting preference or enabling a supported all-node mode repairs only after provisioning. Pending mechanisms: The foundation has generic trunk readiness and route matching but does not model ingress-node membership, cluster call-manager groups or SIP device-handler matching. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:signalling, uc-new:domain:directory-dialplan, uc-new:domain:provisioning.

Candidate observable behavior: A target visible from the new SIP ingress resolves and the IVR continues after staged cutover. Negative boundary: An otherwise existing target outside the new trunk's search scope returns a synthetic not-found result; testing the legacy path separately does not mark the new path healthy. Pending mechanisms: The current dial-plan path has simple ordered routes and permissions but not inherited partition/search-space context or migration comparison between old and new gateway ingress. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:directory-dialplan, uc-new:domain:migration.

Candidate observable behavior: A compatible model/load parses the current configuration and observed time/config generation matches the effective assignment. Negative boundary: An unsupported field or corrupted synthetic config leaves the prior observed generation intact and exposes a parse/model mismatch even though registration remains up. Pending mechanisms: The foundation observes resource readiness and firmware version but does not represent downloaded configuration generations, parsing errors, timezone schema compatibility or observed-vs-effective endpoint settings. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:provisioning, uc-new:domain:discovery.

Candidate observable behavior: A compatible target image installs and post-upgrade checks confirm both registration and display capability. Negative boundary: A rejected upgrade leaves the prior active load registered but marks the display capability failed; a ping/registration check alone cannot pass the device acceptance. Pending mechanisms: The estate pack already proposes firmware compatibility and per-device upgrade status; this thread supports separately tracking active-load registration, inactive-load failure and hardware revision. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:provisioning, uc-new:domain:discovery.

Candidate observable behavior: A supported change sent through the configured management path persists after reset and the room endpoint remains reachable by its canonical URI. Negative boundary: An unsupported local change reverts and an alias pointing at the stale URI fails; do not infer feature parity between CE and TC endpoints. Pending mechanisms: The estate package can track provisioning, and the calling package tracks aliases, but neither currently models room-endpoint capability, authoritative configuration source or SIP-URI identity drift. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:provisioning, uc-new:domain:identity, uc-new:family:cisco:dedicated-premises.

Candidate observable behavior: A phone whose trust bundle accepts the edge chain enrolls and registers; the client and room phone are evaluated independently. Negative boundary: A client succeeds while the phone fails TLS with an explicit trust-chain reason; adding a compatible synthetic trust anchor and reprovisioning enables retry. Pending mechanisms: The core has generic certificates and external connectivity dependencies but not per-endpoint trust roots, activation-code enrollment or separate client-versus-phone MRA capability. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:provisioning, uc-new:domain:signalling, uc-new:family:cisco:dedicated-premises.

Candidate observable behavior: After the required fictional control-plane path is reachable and the inherited object is reconciled, the peer warning clears while service remains available. Negative boundary: A green cluster membership indicator does not hide a failed peer diagnostic; an unconfigured or blocked control path retains a distinct warning and recovery action. Pending mechanisms: Current local infrastructure checks generic DNS/time/certificates, but does not model control-plane packets, cluster peer health, hidden inherited zones or stale provisioned objects. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:signalling, uc-new:domain:continuity, uc-new:family:cisco:dedicated-premises.

Candidate observable behavior: Correctly mapped active rows migrate once, preserve ownership, and remain placed only after target verification. Negative boundary: Inactive or conflicting rows fail independently with retained evidence; retrying after data correction does not duplicate successful rows or overwrite a newer target edit. Pending mechanisms: The estate package proposes staged migration and per-item failure/retry. Current product migration has cohort-level checks but not a source-field mapping audit, inactive-record filtering or uniqueness-conflict queue. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:migration, uc-new:domain:discovery, uc-new:domain:identity.

Candidate observable behavior: A staged upgrade proceeds only after every in-scope endpoint has a supported target path or an explicitly retained compatible service path. Negative boundary: The upgrade is blocked or leaves an explicit failed cohort when a target release drops a device; a successful publisher upgrade alone cannot mark endpoints migrated. Pending mechanisms: The estate package proposes firmware/platform compatibility and rollback; it does not yet require a target-release support audit across hypervisor baseline and endpoint models before starting migration. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:migration, uc-new:domain:provisioning, uc-new:domain:discovery.

Candidate observable behavior: A call between otherwise incompatible tenants succeeds only after selecting an overlapping codec or making a compatible transcoder effective; media evidence names the chosen path. Negative boundary: Both tenants can call a simulated public destination, yet a peer-to-peer call fails with `NO_COMMON_MEDIA` when neither a common codec nor transcoder exists. Pending mechanisms: Current acceptance distinguishes two media directions but does not model codec compatibility across independently administered peer networks or a separately provisioned transcoder.

Candidate observable behavior: A deliberately delayed cancellation produces one deterministic terminal outcome with both legs reconciled and an auditable event trace. Negative boundary: A late response after cancellation must not leave the call marked connected or create a duplicate charge/interaction. Pending mechanisms: The current kernel models call outcomes and traces but not a race between SIP final responses and cancellation across separate legs.

Candidate observable behavior: The learner identifies affected services from observed tests, communicates only confirmed facts, routes through an already validated alternate, and closes only after independent recovery checks pass. Negative boundary: A green status page or an unverified cause hypothesis alone cannot close the incident; a stale successful call cannot prove current recovery. Pending mechanisms: Current faults are resource-scoped and do not model cross-service incident timelines, evidence confidence, or customer-support updates.

Candidate observable behavior: A valid synthetic request reaches the intended tenant, while a request matching the configured unwanted host condition is rejected with the selected response. Negative boundary: A rule that only matches an IP literal does not silently satisfy a request-domain policy; an overbroad filter is detected by a valid-traffic regression case. Pending mechanisms: There is no SIP edge filtering model or acceptance for false positives and explicit signaling response semantics.

Candidate observable behavior: A compatible media policy follows the revised endpoint and both directions become reachable after the re-INVITE. Negative boundary: A 200 response and RTP counters on unrelated legs cannot pass when one expected receiver has no inbound media. Pending mechanisms: Current mechanics can represent one-way media but not media-latching behavior changing during a call after a re-INVITE.

Candidate observable behavior: The learner isolates the failing route with a control call, submits normalized synthetic trace evidence to the correct fictional role, and verifies a repaired call. Negative boundary: An escalation without destination, timestamp, route, and observed failure remains incomplete; an alternate is not treated as available until tested. Pending mechanisms: The current interface has no support ticket lifecycle, escalation evidence bundle, or support-chain dependency.

Candidate observable behavior: A permitted route handles the same synthetic destination from the supported origin region, with the selected carrier and translation visible in the trace. Negative boundary: A route that works from one region cannot be assumed to work from another; unsupported service-area or carrier capability fails with a precise reason. Pending mechanisms: Current route resolution has no origin-region-aware toll-free translation or carrier identifier capability model.

Candidate observable behavior: A selected design meets the declared recovery and support-window constraints, and the test confirms failover through an independent path. Negative boundary: A low-cost design lacking the required support window or independent failure path fails qualification even if its feature checklist is longer. Pending mechanisms: Current product/offer decisions do not grade support coverage, operational skill requirements, or failover independence.

Candidate observable behavior: A portability-corrected synthetic messaging lookup selects the eligible messaging carrier, delivers the test message, and records only a confirmed cost. Negative boundary: A successful voice route cannot imply messaging delivery; a stale lookup or unconfirmed fee cannot be presented as successful/current. Pending mechanisms: The application lacks a messaging-specific portability lookup, lookup freshness, and uncertain charge-notice model.

Candidate observable behavior: A chosen keepalive refreshes the synthetic path before expiry and the endpoint remains callable with bounded signaling overhead. Negative boundary: A stale registration cannot be treated as reachable when its observed connection has expired; the learner must recover registration before incoming calls pass. Pending mechanisms: Current endpoints have registration and connectivity states but do not model idle transport expiry, keepalive layers, or reconnect delay.

Candidate observable behavior: A synthetic service code resolves using the caller's fictional region; the emergency-location test returns the configured synthetic location and callback metadata without contacting a real service. Negative boundary: A missing or stale region mapping fails with an explicit unknown-translation reason; no test input can route to a live emergency destination or be labeled legal compliance. Pending mechanisms: Current emergency handling is an initial synthetic policy and has no dated geography-specific service-code table or isolated location/callback test workflow.
